record.paper_title: Problèmes ouverts en théorie des intersections
record.original_question: Let Y be a closed subset of X and let L be a perfect complex on X whose restriction to X−Y is zero in the derived-category sense, so that the cohomology sheaves of L are supported on Y. Can one define Chern classes with support in Y, c_i^Y(L), lying in cohomology with support H_Y^{2i}(X,Z_ℓ(i)) or in the corresponding ordinary cohomology with support, so that their images under the canonical map to ordinary cohomology recover the general Chern classes of perfect complexes? Can these supported Chern classes be used in a proof or strengthened formulation of cohomological Riemann-Roch, with or without denominators?

evidence.quote: lorsque Y est une partie fermée de X telle que L.|(X-Y) soit nul (au sens des catégories dérivées), i.e. telle que les faisceaux de cohomologie de L. soient à supports dans Y, on aimerait définir des classes de Chern à support dans Y
Il est probable que les classes de Chern avec supports auront un rôle à jouer dans la démonstration de la formule de Riemann-Roch cohomologique sans dénominateurs.
D'autre part, elles devraient permettre de donner une version améliorée de la formule de Riemann-Roch (avec ou sans dénominateurs) en introduisant dans cette formule des familles de supports.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a noetherian scheme (or a sufficiently nice algebraic variety/scheme on which étale cohomology with $\mathbb{Z}_\ell(i)$ coefficients is defined) and let $Y \subseteq X$ be a closed subset with open complement $U = X \setminus Y$. Let $L^\bullet$ be a perfect complex of $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules whose restriction $L^\bullet|_U$ is acyclic (equivalently, zero in the derived category of $U$), so that all cohomology sheaves $\mathcal{H}^j(L^\bullet)$ are supported on $Y$.

(a) Construct, for every $i \geq 0$, Chern classes with support
$$c_i^Y(L^\bullet) \in H_Y^{2i}(X, \mathbb{Z}_\ell(i))$$
(or in the analogous ordinary cohomology with support in $Y$), that are functorial in $(X,Y,L^\bullet)$, additive on distinguished triangles in the appropriate Grothendieck-group sense, and such that under the canonical "forget supports" map
$$H_Y^{2i}(X,\mathbb{Z}_\ell(i)) \longrightarrow H^{2i}(X,\mathbb{Z}_\ell(i))$$
the class $c_i^Y(L^\bullet)$ is sent to the ordinary $i$-th Chern class $c_i(L^\bullet)$ of the perfect complex $L^\bullet$.

(b) Using such classes $c_i^Y(L^\bullet)$, formulate and prove a refined version of the cohomological Grothendieck–Riemann–Roch theorem — both the version with denominators and the version without denominators — that incorporates families of supports, i.e. that takes place naturally in cohomology with support and recovers the usual Riemann–Roch formula after forgetting supports.
artifact.category_tag: Chern classes with support and Riemann-Roch
artifact.status_search_result: Localized/supported Chern classes for perfect complexes acyclic off a closed subset have been constructed in various settings (e.g. via MacPherson-style local Chern character constructions of Baum–Fulton–MacPherson, Iversen, and Bloch, and more recently in motivic/refined Gysin frameworks). The Riemann–Roch theorem without denominators has been proved by Jouanolou and extended into motivic homotopy theory and higher K-theory. However, a fully general formulation incorporating families of supports and giving a strengthened cohomological Riemann–Roch with supports remains an active topic; no single reference appears to settle the question in the broad generality stated.

status_evidence.title: The Riemann–Roch theorem without denominators in motivic homotopy theory
status_evidence.snippet: Proves the Riemann–Roch theorem without denominators for Chern class maps on higher algebraic K-groups in motivic homotopy theory.
status_evidence.claim: Riemann–Roch without denominators is established in the motivic-homotopy framework, but not specifically with families of supports.

status_evidence.title: Chern class and Riemann-Roch theorem for cohomology theory without homotopy invariance
status_evidence.snippet: Formulates axioms for graded cohomology theories with Chern class maps from higher K-theory and proves GRR and Riemann-Roch without denominators.
status_evidence.claim: Higher Chern class versions of Riemann-Roch are established in axiomatic cohomology theories.

status_evidence.title: On the higher Riemann-Roch without denominators
status_evidence.snippet: Develops higher Riemann–Roch without denominators using refined Gysin morphisms and localized Chern classes.
status_evidence.claim: Localized/supported Chern class constructions are used to refine Riemann-Roch.
